description: Per-candidate backfill rows for #56 (track #50). Researched 2026-09-01. He is a two-office officeholder and both offices were searched: elected 12th Ward alderman 2003-2022 (resigned 2022-11-30), then elected Cook County Board of Review commissioner for the 1st District in 2022 - he won that primary and ran UNOPPOSED in the November 2022 general, taking the seat that December - and he has chaired the board since. He won the 2026-03-17 Democratic primary over Juanita Irizarry; say he won the PRIMARY, not that he was re-elected, because the general is November 2026 and has not happened. The chairmanship is confirmed on the agency's own bio page ('in his first term as Chairman of the Cook County Board of Review & Commissioner of the Board of Review's First District'), not inferred from a search summary. So his Board of Review tenure is December 2022 to the present, about three years nine months, which is the window the 2024 op-ed falls in; the 2019 questionnaire is aldermanic-era. Say elected for both - unlike brewer (#57), nothing here is an appointment. WHAT ALREADY EXISTS AND IS NOT RE-RUN: the 2026-06-16 campaign platform pillar (cardenas4chicago.com/pillar-economic-growth.html) is already merged as evidence with 7 statements and it seeded all 5 of his current cells. It is deliberately NOT a row here. Re-extraction is nondeterministic (CLAUDE.md: same article, same model, 0/2/3 statements across runs) and a citation pins a statement INDEX, so re-running it would supersede its own verified citations for no gain. Note also that his platform GRID at cardenas4chicago.com is JS-rendered and raises EmptyTranscriptError (issue #56 warns about this, #30 would fix it); the pillar SUB-PAGE that was already ingested is plain HTML and worked. WHAT WAS SEARCHED. Podcast feeds first, per the #52 lesson: all three feeds in sources.json were pulled and grepped for both spellings. The Ben Joravsky Show has two passing mentions of him in episode descriptions (2022-11-23, 2026-05-09) but no episode with him as guest. City Cast Chicago covered his launch on 2026-06-18 but the guest is a contributor, not the candidate. The Fran Spielman Show has exactly one Cardenas episode, 2021-11-18 'Ald. George Cardenas (12th)', and its own description says the subject is his plan to study the feasibility of the city buying the Chicago Bears plus crime and whether to retain CPD Supt. David Brown. That is an aldermanic-era interview on non-housing subjects, so it is NOT a row; it is the one deliberately unspent source here, and if the mechanism yield below ever looks thin it is the first thing to run. THE REAL DEAL Q&A SERIES, surfaced during #57 and checked here first as that issue instructed: his questionnaire is live (row 7, the last row) and it is the strongest current source. Note its framing honestly - the piece says 'Responses to The Real Deal's questions from the Cardenas' campaign office', i.e. a campaign-office questionnaire response rather than a live interview. Brewer's was the same and shipped; flagging it, not relitigating it. The headline 'would redirect TIFs' is the outlet's, drawn from his platform - the only TIF sentence in his actual answers is that City Hall must show existing housing, TIF, development and homelessness dollars are working before asking for more. Do not let the headline become a stance. THE RECORD, which is what #56 is mostly about. Two distinct bodies of action were found, one per office. (a) 12TH WARD, Parkview Lofts: a 120-unit affordable / 39-unit market-rate conversion of two vacant Central Manufacturing District warehouses at 2139 and 2159 W. Pershing Rd, about 600 feet from the MAT Asphalt plant he had championed. He drove it through all three approval stages in May 2021 - Plan Commission 7-4 (row 3), Zoning Committee 11-3, full City Council 36-13 (row 4) - and is quoted by name at each. This is a rare clean record item: a named alderman, a recorded vote, a housing outcome, and his own words at every step. (b) BOARD OF REVIEW, property-tax circuit breaker: he wrote a signed Sun-Times op-ed (row 5) arguing for income-indexed property-tax relief extended to renters, and briefed the City Council Committee on Housing and Real Estate on statewide circuit-breaker legislation on 2024-09-11 (row 6, Austin Weekly News, covers the same proposal with a direct emailed statement from him). CRITICAL OUTCOME CAUTION, the #57 lesson applied. Parkview Lofts was APPROVED and NEVER BUILT. The city's Department of Housing denied roughly $8 million in financing in August 2020 over the asphalt plant's proximity (row 2, where he is quoted looking for TIF money instead and telling the housing commissioner to 'stay in her lane'); COVID tax-credit relief revived it; the 2021 approvals followed; and in 2023 the developers gave up and listed the buildings for sale. So the record entry for the Council approval is outcome 'enacted' for THE APPROVAL ONLY and its action wording must not imply units exist. The project's 2023 collapse is reported by Crain's, which 403s even from a residential IP and, on the search summary, quotes a developer rather than Cardenas - and he had left the Council by then. There is therefore NO citable 'failed' entry for the collapse and that is stated as a gap rather than written from memory. Likewise the circuit-breaker bill: an Illinois HB3808 exists in the 2025-26 session and has not moved out of subcommittee, but its sponsor is Rep. Justin Slaughter and nothing fetched here ties that specific bill to his proposal, so his advocacy is recorded at what the sources actually establish and no outcome is claimed about a bill he may not own. ROW ORDER IS CHRONOLOGICAL AND DELIBERATE. write_stance is last-write-wins per topic except where the #90 mechanism guard or the #57 polarity guard blocks it, so oldest first lets the most current source have the final say on any cell an earlier row did not fill with a mechanism. Three of his five existing cells carry mechanism null - affordable-housing-funding, permitting-reform, homelessness - so #90 does NOT protect them and any row here can take them; zoning-reform and tenant-protections do carry mechanisms and are protected. TWO COLLISIONS TO CHECK BY HAND IN THE WRITTEN FILES, not to assume. First, polarity: row 1 (2019) has him supporting a real estate transfer tax increase, row 7 (2026) has him declining to revive the transfer tax in the form voters rejected - the exact shape that inverted brewer's cell. Processing 2026 last means the #57 guard should REFUSE the supports-to-opposes flip on affordable-housing-funding and union the citation anyway. Verify that in data/stances/george-cardenas/affordable-housing-funding.json. Second, currency vs specificity: row 1 is a 2019 ALDERMANIC questionnaire and it names real instruments (two-thirds aldermanic approval for TIF porting; a City Council committee hearing for every proposed affordable housing project). Those may take the null-mechanism permitting-reform and property-taxes-tif cells and then #90 will protect a seven-year-old aldermanic-race answer against his 2026 mayoral platform. That is the guard working as designed - specificity beats vagueness, one-way - but it is a currency regression worth reading before the PR opens, and the citations union so both sources stay visible. WHAT WAS EXCLUDED AND WHY. Launch-day press is skipped: the Block Club launch piece was fetched and read in full (4055 chars) and Block Club's own reporter says he 'was light on policy specifics' - his quotes are biography, a parenting stipend and 'fiscal discipline', zero housing, the same shape that produced 0/1 on giannoulias in #52. WTTW's launch piece 403s from a residential IP. The 2026-02-26 Sun-Times/WBEZ Board of Review primary piece was fetched and read (5137 chars, 9 Cardenas mentions) and is NOT a row: every quote of his is about Commissioner Steele, endorsements and his opponent, and the only record sentence ('had done much in office to help homeowners in minority communities fight property tax increases') is reporter narration with no instrument - it would add a weak statement and no mechanism. A 2024-09 Times Weekly item carrying the circuit-breaker detail verbatim is a republished press release, not a media appearance, so it is excluded even though it is the most numerically specific text found ($75,000 income cap, $350,000 assessed value, 5% of income, $5,000 maximum, renters at 20% of annual rent) - rows 5 and 6 carry the same proposal in sources that are actually journalism. A mckinleypark.news op-ed of his (2024, on the city's property-tax levy) is excluded as property-tax-and-budget-only with no housing instrument, the same call that keeps pappas and nee thin. A Crain's op-ed of his 403s. THE OPEN QUESTION THIS CANDIDATE RAISES for the remaining six issues: rows 5 and 1 are an op-ed and a questionnaire the candidate WROTE rather than said. They are first-person and on the record in real outlets, which is why they are in, but they are not 'media appearances' in the interview sense, and row 5 is the single richest mechanism source found for him. Worth a maintainer ruling before quigley/mendoza/johnson, all of whom will have more of this. RUN LOG 2026-09-01. All 7 rows run locally in one pass, in file order; 22 housing statements across 6 evidence files. Row 6 (Austin Weekly News) returned ZERO housing statements and wrote no evidence file. That is the correct call, not a miss: his only words there are an emailed statement about property-tax fairness for working-class households with no housing instrument, the same property-tax-is-not-housing line that keeps pappas and nee thin. One schema-invalid statement was dropped by extract.py (confidence -1) and its valid siblings kept, as designed. YIELD: he goes from 5 cells to 6 (new: property-taxes-tif) and from 2 named mechanisms to 4. LOCAL REVIEW: all 6 evidence files were run through `python -m pipeline review` on the same residential IP that fetched them (the hosted reviewer returns unverifiable for these, #69). Result 22/22 confirmed, label ai-verified, no flags. WHAT THE RUN SETTLED ABOUT THE GUARDS, which is the part worth carrying to the remaining six issues. (1) The #57 polarity guard was NOT exercised, and I only know that because I read the written file. The Real Deal statement #8 ('I would not revive the transfer tax proposal in the form Chicago voters rejected') extracted as affordable-housing-funding / opposes at confidence 1.0 — the brewer inversion shape exactly — but it never became the proposal, because _rank puts mechanism-bearing statements first and #8 names none. It lost a tie-break, not a guard. That is the second candidate in a row where a transfer-tax answer was stopped by _rank rather than by the polarity guard, which strengthens rather than closes the stance-label question #57 opened. (2) The specificity regression is real and the code cannot see it. Two of his existing cells already carried a mechanism, so #90 did not apply and last-write-wins replaced both with VAGUER text from the newer source: zoning-reform went from 'as-of-right housing near CTA/Metra, bus corridors, and commercial districts' plus neighborhood typologies to bare 'as-of-right housing growth', and tenant-protections went from 'legal aid, rental help, and preservation funds' to 'antidisplacement safeguards' — the latter taken from a sentence that is really about zoning and was mis-filed to tenant-protections. #90 guards mechanism-vs-null; it does not guard specific-vs-vague when both sides name something. Worth considering whether that is a gap or an acceptable limit. HAND CORRECTIONS, in the brewer 'corrected by hand' sense — cells only, NO evidence file was edited. zoning-reform and tenant-protections were restored to their platform summaries and mechanisms (unioned citations kept, so the newer source stays visible). affordable-housing-funding was moved off The Real Deal statement #1 to statement #6: #1 is the reporter's platform-summary sentence ('redirecting one of developer's favorite tools: tax increment financing resources') while #6 is his own first-person answer ('stronger production targets for deeply affordable units'), and where both name a mechanism the candidate's own words should carry the cell. NOTE that the reviewer confirmed #1 as his platform and did NOT flag it, so unlike brewer's statement #9 there was no two-model agreement to justify deleting it; it stays in evidence and stays cited. property-taxes-tif was moved off The Real Deal statement #9 to the Sun-Times circuit-breaker op-ed: #9 answers a question about downtown OFFICE assessments, the weakest housing link available, while the circuit breaker is his signature named instrument and is argued explicitly in terms of housing affordability and renters. Both citations are kept on the cell either way. THE RECORD: one entry, on permitting-reform. Filed there rather than affordable-housing-funding because the action is an aldermanic-prerogative call on a development, which is that topic's description and #56's own wording; the funding for this project was denied, so it is not a funding action. Wording is deliberately 'urged … approve' and 'the City Council approved the redevelopment 36-13', because outcome 'enacted' here means THE APPROVAL was enacted. Parkview Lofts was never built: the developers listed the buildings for sale in 2023 after the city and state financing never materialised. That collapse is reported by Crain's, which 403s from a residential IP, and on the search summary it quotes a developer rather than Cardenas, who had left the Council by then. So there is NO citable 'failed' entry and the record does not claim one — the same 'a missing outcome is a finding' call as brewer's HUD litigation. BOARD OF REVIEW RECORD: none, and this is a coverage finding rather than un-run work. His circuit-breaker briefing to the City Council Committee on Housing and Real Estate on 2024-09-11 is documented only in a republished press release, which is not a media appearance; the Sun-Times op-ed is a POSITION (now on the property-taxes-tif cell) rather than an action; Austin Weekly yielded nothing citable. An Illinois HB3808 circuit-breaker bill exists in the 2025-26 session and has not moved out of subcommittee, but its sponsor is Rep. Justin Slaughter and nothing fetched here ties it to his proposal, so no outcome is asserted about a bill he may not own. Aldermanic votes on the 2021 ARO rewrite and the 2022 Connected Communities ordinance were searched and produced no coverage quoting him, so they are absent rather than excluded. MAINTAINER RULING 2026-09-02: op-eds and questionnaires the candidate AUTHORED are accepted sources, here and for every remaining candidate. The open question raised above is closed - rows 1 and 5 stand, and the remaining issues should actively search for this source class rather than treat it as a borderline case. ADDENDUM 2026-09-02, rows 8-9, and the Board of Review record question. ROW 8 (Crain's op-ed) exists because the maintainer supplied the saved page: Crain's 403s every IP tried, residential and Anthropic's alike, so the bytes were served to process_source through the injected `fetcher` seam - same extractor, same quote-in-transcript guard, same reviewer, no hand-written statements. It is genuinely distinct from his 2024-11-09 mckinleypark.news op-ed on adjacent subject matter: 7 housing statements, 7/7 confirmed locally, and it corroborates the circuit breaker from a second outlet a year after the Sun-Times piece. Date 2025-07-29 read off the saved page, not a search summary. ROW 9 ANSWERS THE BOARD OF REVIEW RECORD QUESTION, and how it was reached matters more than the row. The question asked was whether the board systematically reducing commercial assessments - downtown parking garages was the example - shifts burden onto homeowners and should count against his record. The reasoning is sound and the pattern is real and measurable: Cook County's `Board of Review Appeal Decision History` (7pny-nedm) shows tax year 2024 commercial classes taking far larger reductions than residential (class 593 -14.9%, 517 -8.5%, 590 -8.0%, against -0.8% to -4.8% across residential classes). But that analysis CANNOT become a record entry, for three independent reasons, and the third is the one that would survive fixing the other two. (1) A record entry cites "<evidence-id>#<index>", i.e. a quote from a media source; an analysis run here is original research with no outlet behind it - Golden Rule 3. (2) NO published Cook County dataset attributes a decision to a commissioner: 7pny-nedm is parcel-level with result, values, appellant and attorney but no commissioner and no vote; pfs5-q57r is district-boundary geography only; the two aggregate datasets stop at 2010, before his tenure. The board certifies appeals as an institution, so there is no roll call to publish. (3) Even a perfect district-scoped analysis would attribute an institutional pattern to one of three commissioners - exactly the #49 trap ('the CHA did X' vs 'Brewer said X') this repo has already been burned by. A related caution: the district map in pfs5-q57r is the 2010-census map and is STALE - it places McKinley Park, where he lives and which he represents, in District 2 rather than his District 1 - so it cannot be used to decide whether downtown falls in his district. Do not scope anything to a commissioner with it. THE RESOLUTION is that the argument is already published and he is on the record answering it. Cook County Treasurer Maria Pappas's report (WBEZ / Chicago Sun-Times, 2025-05-05, row 9) makes precisely the burden-shift case - $25.5bn in business valuation reductions against $1.9bn added to homeowners' bills - and the Assessor's office says directly that 'big businesses received outsized reductions from the Cook County Board of Review'. Cardenas DENIES it on the record. That denial is citable where a statistic is not. ROW 9 REQUIRED THE SANCTIONED MANUAL EXTRACTION, and the reason is a finding. THREE real extractor runs on that page returned only the reporter's TIF-and-assessments fragment (housing counts 2, 1, 2) and never once surfaced his two direct quotes, which are the entire value of the source. Worse, the fragment it did return kept landing as `opposes` with mechanism 'government spending cutbacks' and hijacking the property-taxes-tif cell. So the two verbatim quotes were supplied through a hand-authored statements payload per CLAUDE.md's fallback - the quote-in-transcript guard, the schema check and the candidate/topic filter all still ran, both quotes passed, and the reviewer independently confirmed 2/2. Note what this says about the extractor: it is tuned to policy proposals and reliably misses a candidate DEFENDING HIS OWN AGENCY against a criticism, which is a shape the record work needs and daily discovery would silently drop. THE CELL HAD TO BE RESTORED BY HAND A THIRD AND FOURTH TIME. property-taxes-tif lost 'property tax circuit breaker program, extended to renters' to bare 'circuit breaker' (row 8) and then to 'government spending cutbacks' (row 9). That is four hand corrections of the same #90 specific-vs-vague hole on one candidate. It is no longer an edge case.
